title: HTMLOrSVGElement.focus() implies that the element should be scrolled into view when it isn't a focusable area

labels.name: needs tests
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires someone to write tests

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

The text of https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#dom-focus states:

> The [HTMLOrSVGElement](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#htmlorsvgelement) focus(options) method steps are:
> 
>  1. If the [allow focus steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#allow-focus-steps) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [node document](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document) return false, then return.
>  2. Run the [focusing steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#focusing-steps) for [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).
>  3. If options["focusVisible"] is true, or does not [exist](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-exists) but in an [implementation-defined](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined) way the user agent determines it would be best to do so, then [indicate focus](https://drafts.csswg.org/selectors/#indicate-focus).
>  4. If options["preventScroll"] is false, then [scroll a target into view](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom-view/#scroll-a-target-into-view) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), "auto", "center", and "center".

Step 1 & 2 of the focusing steps are:

> If new focus target is not a [focusable area](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#focusable-area), then set new focus target to the result of [getting the focusable area](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#get-the-focusable-area) for new focus target, given focus trigger if it was passed.
> 
> 2 If new focus target is null, then:
>    1. If no fallback target was specified, then return.
>    2. Otherwise, set new focus target to the fallback target.

This means that the focusing steps might focus a different target other than `this` or not focus anything at all. Yet, step 3 and 4 happen no matter what happened while the focusing steps ran. This means that if `focus()` is called on an element that is not a focusable area, the specification implies that the user agent should scroll to the element even if it was not focused. I don't think any browser does this.
